#1 [samhan] Queen Sunduk / 선덕여왕 (632) tone=royal court drama
  P1: A Queen? Ridiculous.
  P2: Munhee (26) is a young noblewoman, being attended by her low-rank servants. She is getting her hair done for an important event, while a servant takes care of her baby son Inmun (3).
  P3: Her husband Chunchu is dressing too. He is twenty-nine, and already the most cunning man in Samhan. Only the quiet rooms know it yet. Their two children are getting under everyone's feet.
  Q: The sacred-bone males were exhausted, and therefore a queen was set up.
#2 [samhan] Harmony Council / 화백회의 (632) tone=chamber deliberation drama
  P1: The Harmony Council meets to debate who the next king should be. Six nobles, one night. Nobody stands up until they all agree.
  P2: Night in a small pavilion off the pond. Someone lights the small brazier. The flame is red first.
  P3: It runs hotter. The flame turns blue. Only then may the session start.
  Q: Every matter must be discussed by all of them together. They call it the Hwabaek, the Harmony Council. If one man dissents, the matter is dropped.
#3 [samhan] Jinheung, the Cloud / 진흥왕, <법운> (554) tone=fairy-tale legend
  P1: Ask anyone in Surabol about the Cloud King and they'll tell you about his stones. Ask anyone in Sabi and they'll change the subject. You'll find out why. Not yet.
  P2: He was seven when they put the crown on him. It was too big, and nobody mentioned it. By the end, Silla had a river, a coastline and Gaya. He got there by being the best ally in Samhan, right up until the afternoon he wasn't.
  P3: He put up stones wherever he stopped — four of them, on mountains, at the edges of what he had taken — and the stones do not boast. They say who came, and when, and that the land is now inside the border. They are property deeds.
  Q: On the twenty-first day of the eighth month, in the first year of Taechang, the Great King Jinheung toured the lands in his keeping, and had this cut into stone
#4 [samhan] Prince Euija / 의자태자 (632) tone=palace coming-of-age
  P1: Thirty-two is late to be named crown prince. By the time his father gets around to it, Euija has more than fifteen sons. The clans have had years to decide which ones they own.
  P2: In Sabi the clans read the stars the way other courts read ledgers. Loyalty is the word they use when the door between king and house is still closed; after it opens, they use other words.
  P3: This is said admiringly. It is that kind of court.
  Q: He served his parents with filial piety and treated his brothers with fraternal love; in his time he was called the Zengzi of the East of the Sea.
#5 [samhan] Eight Great Clans / 대성팔족 (632) tone=clan face-off (shonen)
  P1: Satek. Yunbi. Jinmo. Mokli. Hae. Baek. Guk. Ahn.
  P2: The Eight Great Clans run this country, and one king sits between them. Satek fights with the king's sleeve. Yunbi fights with the coast road. The other six keep their techniques quiet.
  P3: Once a year, the court chalks a square grid in the palace yard. Four hard lines. No banners. The young men of each house step onto the grid in white. It's the same quarrel as the west bridge, only without the carts.
  Q: The great surnames of the country are eight clans: Sa, Yeon, Hyeop, Hae, Jin, Guk, Mok and Baek.
#6 [samhan] Gunchogo, the 13th / 근초고왕 (371) tone=fairy-tale legend
  P1: Baekje’s thirteenth king marches north to Pyongyang. A Goguryeo king dies on his own wall. In seven hundred years, it never happens again.
  P2: Baekje has the river, the coast and the sea roads east. The clans take the docks. The throne takes a cut. It is the richest kingdom in Samhan, and the strongest. Neither lasts.
  P3: They will still be chanting that sentence three centuries later, in a courtyard, to a clever king who has already decided that a country is a story. It is the sentence that gets Daeya burned.
  Q: In winter the king and the crown prince led thirty thousand picked troops into Goguryeo and attacked Pyongyang. The Goguryeo king, Sayu, fought hard to hold the
#7 [samhan] Commander Yeon / 연개소문 (634) tone=frontier military drama
  P1: In the high mountains of Manchuria, a young man is caught in the snow by a Goguryeo soldier.
  P2: He is taken to the outpost of Commander Yeon (29), the Eternal General — a ruthless military general.
  P3: It is over quickly, and it is not clean. Nobody in the yard looks away, because looking away is also a report.
  Q: Gaesomun*, also called Gaegeum. His surname was Yeon. He claimed he had been born in water, to awe the crowd. He was imposing to look at, and bold and free in s
#8 [samhan] High Summit / 제가회의 (634) tone=summit theater
  P1: So Yeon rides to Pyongyang in his father's place. Five commanders, one king, one room. They call it the High Summit.
  P2: He rides in at the red two-tier gate. Pyongyang already knows the sound of those hooves.
  P3: Goguryeo works like this. Five commanders argue. The High Commander holds the first sword. The king has the last word.
  Q: Their highest office is called Daedaero, the High Commander. It ranks with our first grade, and its holder oversees all the business of the state. It changes ha
#9 [samhan] Gwanggaeto, the Great King / 광개토대왕 (400) tone=fairy-tale legend
  P1: Silla is drowning. An army from across the sea is inside its walls. Then Gwanggaeto sends fifty thousand horsemen south, and the Wa are gone.
  P2: A red sun. The three-legged crow rides south on his banners. The stele will list sixty-four fortresses. It will not list the nerve it took.
  P3: Sixty-four fortresses, one reign. The stele at his tomb lists them all.
  Q: The common people were at peace in their work; the country was rich and the people abundant; the five grains ripened in plenty.
#10 [five-principles] Bupmin / 김법민 (641) tone=young-adult academy (Hwarang)
  P1: It is the spring Bupmin turns fifteen.
  P2: The Hwarang train under the Marshal: horse, bow, verse, and above all gyuku, a horse-ball game a lazier age will call polo.
  P3: Bupmin (15) is old enough for the headband and too young to invent a country alone. His father is in the Council chamber collecting votes. His uncle keeps the yard.
  Q: Bupmin was striking in bearing, quick of mind, and full of strategy.
#11 [five-principles] Sadaham / 사다함 (641) tone=campfire tale (Hwarang)
  P1: Every yard has its ghosts. This one has two, and they have never missed roll call.
  P2: The lamps go up under the eaves. Nobody sends the boys to bed. They decide this is an honour, and they are right, though not for the reason they think.
  P3: The Marshal does not let trust among friends stay a pretty line. He tells the new boys of the first class — the two names the yard still lowers its voice for.
  Q: Ninth month. Gaya rebelled. The king ordered Isabu to punish it, with Sadaham as his second. Sadaham rode ahead with five thousand horse, went in through the Je
#12 [five-principles] Gotaso / 김고타소 (641) tone=K-drama romance
  P1: A young girl is going to do what she’s going to do.
  P2: It begins two springs earlier, with a girl who is not where she is supposed to be.
  P3: Gotaso (16) goes out to the lantern market with two maids and does not come back with any. The maids are found first, by the river, in the morning.
  Q: They wear no powder and no brow-black. Most wind their beautiful hair around the head and dress it with pearls and coloured silk.
#13 [five-principles] Pumsuk / 품석 (641) tone=K-drama romance
  P1: Princess Gotaso (16) has fallen in love with the Hwarang Pumsuk (23), and the whole court can see it before either of them admits the word. The maids keep score of the accidental meetings. The guards move their posts to give the flowering trees more privacy th
  P2: Her parents Chunchu (38) and Munhee (35) bless the marriage. Then, over his wife’s one quiet objection, the father asks the boy for a vow — a vow no father should make his daughter hear.
  P3: He makes him swear. It is the only time in this record that Chunchu misreads a room, and it is the room with his daughter in it.
  Q: Their wedding rites are only wine and food, more or less according to wealth. On the wedding night the bride bows first to her husband's parents, and then to he

#16 [five-principles] Stele / 광개토대왕릉비 (641) tone=house succession drama
  P1: Yeon takes his sons to see the Great King's stone. It lists everything he ever took.
  P2: Every Goguryeo boy is raised on him. He kept the west shut, and he made it look easy.
  P3: Late in the year, old Dosuryu walks in without taking off his boots. In thirty years he has never once done that…!
  Q: In all, the fortresses he attacked and broke: sixty-four. Villages: one thousand four hundred.
#17 [five-principles] Dosuryu / 도수류 (641) tone=conspiracy thriller
  P1: Late in the year Dosuryu comes in without knocking, which he has done since Gesomun was small enough to lift by the collar, and without taking his boots off, which he has never done.
  P2: Yeon stops laughing. He does it all at once, the way a door shuts.
  P3: Dosuryu goes out the way he came in, boots and all, and stands a long time in the yard before he can make himself mount. He has known the boy for thirty years. He knows exactly what kind of list it will be.
  Q: The king ordered Gaesomun, Great Man of the Eastern Division, to oversee the work on the long wall.

#20 [five-principles] The Severing / 단 (斷) (553–554) tone=fairy-tale legend, dark
  P1: The sad thing about betrayal… is that it never comes from your enemies.
  P2: Two kings take a river back together. One is Seong of Baekje. The other is the Cloud King. The deal is simple. Baekje gets the river mouth, near the sea. Silla gets the upper valley.
  P3: For a while the two banners still fly side by side. Then the Cloud King turns his army on Baekje's half. He takes the river mouth and gives it a new name. He fills it with men who won't ask what the alliance meant.
  Q: On the ninth day of the twelfth month I sent them to attack Silla. First I sent Mononobe no Makamu, commander of the Eastern Region, with that region's soldiers
#21 [iron-will] Gumil / 검일 (642) tone=K-drama tragedy
  P1: Before Daeya — before the year that will stain his hands — the Sword of Silla rides alone to a small cavern lake in the hills: a bowl of black water under stone, cold enough to teach the bones manners. He has heard of the place the way a son hears of a hill hi
  P2: The marshal’s robe falls at the rock lip before the steam has a name for him. Confucian blue on wet stone. He does not look up; looking up would be a request.
  P3: Steam lifts. They are already on the far rock: Narim with her ankles crossed like an elder sister who has seen this entrance before; Golhwa legs spread wide in the mist, chima hiked, as if the mist owed her heat; Hyullé a half-step behind them, knees pressed, 
  Q: Silla uses men by bone rank. If you are not of the right lineage, then however great your talent and however outstanding your deeds, you cannot rise past it.
#22 [iron-will] Maehwa / 매화 (642) tone=K-drama tragedy
  P1: A man is measured by his self-control.
  P2: He goes back. The families have thinned. The screen is cheaper in this hour. She is still there. She sits as if she knew he would fail the pallet.
  P3: She drops beside him before he has stood. She sits like the chair was always hers. Jeogori already a little open — not court, not accident. The smirk shows teeth. His mouth is already open and he has not used it yet.
  Q: Before this, the commander Pumsuk had seen that the wife of his staff officer, the saji Gumil, was beautiful, and took her. Gumil resented it.
#23 [iron-will] Siege of Daeya / 대야성 (642) tone=K-drama tragedy
  P1: Grey in the door-slit. The feast is a cold hall. Gumil comes back from the stores and finds his wife where the True Bone left her — dirtied green still open, last night still on the boards. He does not ask if she is hurt. He asks for the story.
  P2: They stand in the door-slit of morning and do not touch. The heat from the feast is gone. What is left is the count of what she said, and the count of what he made her say, and a marriage that has already finished speaking.
  P3: That is the last thing they ever say to each other.
  Q: My father named me Jukjuk so that I would not wither in the cold season, and might be broken but never bent. How should I fear death and live by surrendering?

  P3: October cold sits under the eaves. The lamps are already lit when the Five Commanderies take their seats — wine first, then meat, then the old joke that Pyongyang never runs out of either. Each commander wears a ring-pommel sword at his hip, the three-legged c
  Q: He wore five swords on his body, and no one around him dared look up at him. Every time he mounted or dismounted, he made nobles and generals lie on the ground 
#25 [iron-will] Chunchu & Yeon / 자의악마 (642) tone=enemy-parley thriller
  P1: Since Daeya fell, Chunchu has had one request for the Queen: send him north to Pyongyang, to beg Goguryeo for troops against Baekje. She has not said yes.
  P2: The news reaches Surabol about a month late, the way news from the north usually does.
  P3: Chunchu asks again, and this time the Queen lets him go. Nobody offers to go instead.
  Q: Chunchu secretly gave three hundred measures of blue cloth to the king’s favourite, Seon Dohae.
#26 [iron-will] Euija & Yeon / 해동증자 (642) tone=summit intrigue
  P1: News of Yeon’s Massacre reaches Baekje.
  P2: He asks for troops. He asks twice.
  P3: Yeon is surprised that the new King of Baekje has come personally.
  Q: Eighth month. Baekje also plotted with Goguryeo to take Danghang Fortress and cut off the road to Tang.

  P3: He rides back to his father’s command post, gets down, and takes off his helmet, which is how a son asks permission in front of an army.

#29 [iron-will] The Eastern Star / 동쪽 별 (642) tone=war-legend chronicle
  P1: He touches the left side of his neck when he says it, where the old burn scar runs down under his collar.
  P2: The banquet hall has been scrubbed for three nights. Yeon climbs to a cave in the hill above the river. Nobody prays there lightly. The marches say the stone still remembers bowstrings.
  P3: He kneels at the mouth and lays a crow-stamped ring-pommel on the stone. He does not ask forgiveness for the hall. He asks for witnesses.
  Q: East of the capital there is a great cave called the Sacred Tunnel. Every tenth month the king sacrifices there himself.

  P2: The spat is this: Goguryeo raided the western commandery, the empire sent a general called Guanqiu Jian to explain why that was a mistake, and Goguryeo met him at the Boiling River and won, and then won again.
  P3: So the king took five thousand horse out to win a third time, on ground he had not looked at, and lost eighteen thousand men in an afternoon.

#36 [seventh-invasion] Ansi / 안시성 (645) tone=epic war — the siege
  P1: The Guardian of Ansi Fortress is an eccentric man. When Yeon took the country, the Guardian refused him to his face. He kept the old king’s colours on the wall. Yeon had drowned a whole court for less. He looked at that wall, weighed the siege, and rode away. 
  P2: Nobody writes his name down. To the people inside the walls he is just the chief, and that turns out to be enough.
  P3: The ring at his hip is Goguryeo iron — a hollow circle the same red as the wall.
  Q: Had [the Grand Minister] been alive, he would not have let me make this expedition.

#39 [seventh-invasion] Jolbon / 졸본 (-37) tone=founder fairy tale

  P2: He looks past the spear. The pine behind the man is a better door than the man’s face.

#41 [chunchu-era] Suro / 가야 연맹 (42) tone=founder fairy tale
  P1: Before there is a Gaya, there is a ridge, and a sky god who looks at it too long.
  P2: Before the sons, there is a look from very high up. Ibiga keeps the sky the way other gods keep a hall — cloud is his body, the living world a map he does not usually read. Then he looks down.
  P3: On her mountain the Lady of the Right View is on watch. At first she is the ridge — jade stone, mist, a woman’s shape the mountain has not admitted yet. The mountain is a woman before it has a face. Then a face comes out of the stone. She is guarding the mount
  Q: Turtle, turtle — show your head. If you do not, we will roast and eat you.

  P1: For five hundred years the people of Gaya lived by iron and by six eggs, and they enjoyed great peace.

#46 [chunchu-era] Gyeol (結) / 결 (結) (647) tone=political thriller — countdown

#52 [chunchu-era] Jahee / 김자희 (644) tone=harbour romance (K-drama)

  P2: Her name is Jahee. Tonight she is the daughter who keeps Seonpum’s inkstones, and she has already decided his arithmetic is sloppy.

#53 [chunchu-era] Hyukgose / 혁거세 거서간 (-57) tone=founder fairy tale
  P1: After the fall of Old Joseon, the local chiefs gather to select a new king when a White Horse suddenly leaves an egg — blue sky above, and later the court will keep the moon as its quiet sign.
  P2: At a well in the hills, the horse knelt and cried. Six chiefs dug where it stood. They lifted out a great egg. The shell opened on a boy who already looked like a king. He learns fast. The chiefs say the land has been waiting.
  P3: A young boy is born from the egg, whom the chiefs name Hyukgosé — to rule with brightness — and crown as king while he is still a boy; tradition says thirteen.
  Q: A white horse knelt and cried aloud; they dug the ground and found a great blue egg. They opened it, and there was a boy-child; they named him Hyeokgeose.

#79 [final-stand] Snake River / 사수 전투 (662) tone=grim war epic
  P1: The White Tiger drives his host into the Snake River. They still believe rivers are roads. Yeon Gesomun has been waiting for a man who thinks that. Old men in the north remember another river that ate an army. The Snake is younger. It's hungrier. And it has Ye
  P2: The river does not take them in a heap. Yeon counts. Chang’an’s clerks will later write thirteen sons as if a number were a grave. It is a morning. The water is February-cold and already learning names.
  P3: The thirteenth and the twelfth come together at the first bend — brothers who still share a horse’s width. Yeon meets them in the shallows where the current lies. One stroke. Two bodies. The horse walks on a few steps with no one left to tell it to stop.
  Q: [The White Tiger] fought Yeon Gaesomun on the Snake River; the whole army was lost, and he and his thirteen sons all died in battle.

#84 [final-stand] Yeon Gesomun† / 연개소문, 죽다 (665) tone=deathbed drama
  P1: The Eternal General is dying.
  P2: He expects one of them — Kangrim with his Question, or Haewonmek with his last words. He has been rehearsing a refusal.
  P3: It is not either of them. Purple of sentence, not crow-dark of the fetch — Yumla himself stands in the room. The judge, not the clerks. A king for a king.
  Q: You brothers, be as close as fish and water. Do not quarrel over rank. If you do not heed this, you will surely be the laughingstock of your neighbours.

#93 [silla-tang-war] Kim Yushin† / 김유신, 죽다 (673) tone=psychopomp elegy
  P1: Old now, between campaigns that are mostly paperwork, Yushin still finds the cavern. The steam is thinner. The three are not. They look the same age they always looked — which is either mercy or mockery, and he has never asked which.
  P2: Hyullé’s hand finds the water beside the ledge where he always sits, and stays there. Fifty years of the same ledge.
  P3: The steam thins. For a breath his father’s mouth is in the water — not the counsel, only the name — and then it is steam again.
  Q: I humbly pray Your Highness know that to succeed is not easy, and to keep what has been won is also hard. Keep petty men far and good men near.

#97 [silla-tang-war] The King for All / 삼한왕검 (676) tone=hard-won resolution
  P1: Bupmin, King Munmu now, stands where a six-year-old once stole a sentence. The war is won, the ally has been shown the door, and the childhood dream has had the bad manners to come true.
  P2: It ends where it began: a woman in a room, getting someone else ready.
  P3: Munhee is seventy. She is the last person alive who remembers all of it from the inside, and she is straightening her son's collar. She was twenty-six when this story started. Her sister burned a skirt on a hill so that she could be married.
  Q: After I am gone I wish to become a great dragon that guards the country, to uphold the Buddha’s law and protect the realm.
